name: crt-warp

frames.best_why: Fills the screen with the blocky violet plasma in a balanced tangle of bright patches and black gaps.

tagline: Blocky purple plasma churns behind scanlines like a glowing old monitor.
summary: A full-bleed animated background of coarse violet pixels on black, seen through a curved CRT screen with scanlines, glow and grain. It powers on, then flows and bends toward the pointer.
appearance: The entire stage is a stepped grid of bright violet shapes on black, each edge a square pixel rather than a smooth curve. Fine horizontal scanlines and a soft bloom sit over the blob pattern, with darkened rounded screen edges.
behaviour: The picture starts nearly black and brightens as the grid reveals itself, then the plasma shapes keep merging and drifting. Moving the pointer warps the field near the cursor, and a click rolls the screen and switches to a new pattern.
use_when: A full-bleed backdrop for a retro, synthwave or gaming landing page that wants strong atmosphere.
avoid_when: The busy high-contrast motion fights any text placed over it, and the always-on shader costs GPU time.
customise: Props set ink and paper colours, speed, variation, level and column counts, curvature, scanlines, mask, bloom and pointer response. Changing the plasma shape needs a shader edit.
weight_why: Several full-screen WebGL passes, including a two-direction glow blur, redrawn every frame.

a11y.note: Reduced motion stops the drift and intro, but the click-to-change pattern has no focusable or keyboard path.

issues: The opening frame is almost pure black, so the effect takes a moment to become visible.
polish_why: Convincing CRT look with coherent glow, grain and scanlines; coarse pixel steps are intended.
